claims.text: The local release groups Bulbapedia raw source rows 123-125 under the promotion note Tropical Mega Battle: Dugtrio Team Battle.
The source group contains three modeled rows: Moltres phone card 123, Articuno phone card 124, and Zapdos phone card 125.
The local release boundary is source-derived from the exact Bulbapedia promotion/distribution note and is not official product-boundary proof.

Bulbapedia describes the Tropical Mega Battle as a TCG tournament held annually from 1999 through 2001 in Honolulu, while the local row group carries a mixed-source release date and a Dugtrio Team Battle promotion note. Treat the wider event context as context, not row-level distribution proof.

Pokumon collector pages describe the legendary bird phone cards as given out at Dugtrio Team Battle events including Tropical Mega Battle, Regional Kamex Mega Battle, and Challenge Road events during 1998-1999; this is collector context, not an official distribution census.
The local raw rows do not surface illustrator credits for these phone-card rows; artist or source-art claims should remain unresolved unless supported by card-specific evidence.

Elite Fourum discussion connects the legendary bird phone-card artwork to broader GB-art/prototype-like legendary bird context. This is useful collector texture only and must not be promoted to official row authority.

This source group matters because it is not a normal card trio: it is the legendary birds translated into phone-card tournament memory, where the collectible object is adjacent to play, travel, event attendance, and prize culture.

Agents should preserve row 123/124/125 identity, Phone Card type, exact Tropical Mega Battle: Dugtrio Team Battle promotion note, legendary-bird subject, non-card object status, and unresolved artist credit before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Tropical Mega Battle Dugtrio Team Battle — legendary birds as phone-card event memory
narrative.why_it_matters: This slice is beautiful because it sits slightly outside the ordinary card binder. Moltres, Articuno, and Zapdos are unmistakable TCG gravity, but here the object type is phone card and the route is tournament/event culture. That changes everything. The agent has to see the legendary-bird allure while refusing the easy shortcut: these are not Fossil birds, not vending birds, not ordinary promos with attacks and HP. They are phone-card artifacts grouped by a Dugtrio Team Battle promotion note, part of the wider Tropical Mega Battle/Kamex/Challenge Road collector fog. The romance is real, but the boundary has to be sharper than the romance.
